pattern_name: Advanced and impersonal passive (it is thought that …)
pattern_name_ar: المبني للمجهول المتقدّم وغير الشخصي (it is thought that …)
formula: It + is/was + reporting verb + that + clause · Subject + is said/thought/known + to + verb · Subject + is thought + to have + participle · Long chains: is being + participle, has been + participle, will have been + participle
formula_visual: [It is believed] [that the practice began earlier] · [He is thought] [to have left]
when_to_use: To report information without naming its source, which is the default voice of academic writing, news and formal reports. 'It is believed that …' introduces a whole clause. 'He is said to be …' moves the subject to the front. Add 'have' for a past event: 'He is thought to have left.' Use it when the source is unknown, unimportant, or deliberately unstated.
when_to_use_ar: لنقل معلومة دون تسمية مصدرها، وهو الأسلوب الافتراضي للكتابة الأكاديمية والأخبار والتقارير الرسمية. و'have' تُضاف لحدث ماضٍ. يُستخدم عندما يكون المصدر مجهولًا أو غير مهم.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic reports impersonally with active forms (يُقال إنّ / يُعتقد أنّ) that need no chain of auxiliaries, so English chains such as 'is thought to have been' feel top-heavy and are often shortened incorrectly. Two errors recur: omitting 'to' in the personal pattern ('He is said be rich'), and using a base verb instead of a participle after 'have' ('is thought to have leave'). Learners also mix the two frames into 'It is thought him to have left'.

examples.en: It is believed that the practice began much earlier.
examples.ar: يُعتقد أن هذه الممارسة بدأت في وقت أبكر

examples.en: The building is said to be four hundred years old.
examples.ar: يُقال إن المبنى عمره أربعمئة سنة

examples.en: He is thought to have left the country in 1938.
The proposal is being considered at the highest level.
The work will have been completed by then.
examples.ar: سيكون العمل قد أُنجز بحلول ذلك الوقت

common_errors.wrong: He is said be very wealthy.
common_errors.correct: He is said to be very wealthy.
common_errors.explanation: The personal reporting passive always keeps 'to' before the verb.

common_errors.wrong: He is thought to have leave early.
common_errors.correct: He is thought to have left early.
common_errors.explanation: After 'to have' the verb takes its third form.

common_errors.wrong: It is thought him to have left.
common_errors.correct: It is thought that he left. / He is thought to have left.
common_errors.explanation: Choose one frame: 'It is thought that + clause' or 'Subject + is thought to + verb'.

common_errors.wrong: It is believed the practice began earlier.
common_errors.correct: It is believed that the practice began earlier.
common_errors.explanation: In formal writing keep 'that' after the reporting verb for clarity.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: It ___ (believe) that the report was never sent.
She is said ___ refused the offer twice.
The matter is ___ (investigate) internally at the moment.
He is thought to have ___ (leave) before midnight.

quick_rule: It is + reporting verb + THAT + clause. Or Subject + is said/thought + TO + verb. Add TO HAVE + third form for the past.
quick_rule_ar: It is + فعل النقل + THAT + جملة. أو الفاعل + is said/thought + TO + فعل. وأضف TO HAVE + التصريف الثالث للماضي.
mnemonic: No source needed — the reporting verb carries the claim.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 5 you drilled reduced auxiliary chains with the stress on the final participle. Say 'is thought to have LEFT' with /tə əv/ blurred, or the sentence sounds like a legal document read word by word.
